evidence_set: Four randomised trials, 284 participants: Avila 2024 (USA, 45 people: pouch, e-cigarette, no intervention); Caldwell 2010 (New Zealand, 63, cross-over of pouch, snus and nicotine gum, adverse events only); NCT04250727 (USA, 30: higher against lower strength, registry record only); Rensch 2023 (USA, 146, tobacco-industry funded: pouches of three strengths against a no-tobacco group and a continue-smoking group). All enrolled adults who smoked; three enrolled people not planning to quit; follow-up 7 days to 8 weeks. Ten ongoing studies are listed.

Results › Description of studies › Results of the search; Included studies, Table 4 (overview), Study types, Participants, Interventions and comparators, Outcomes, Funding; Table 5 (per-study participant numbers)

Pouch against minimal control, abstinence at week 8: 1 of 18 given pouches had quit against 0 of 9 with no intervention; RR 1.58 (0.07 to 35.32), 1 trial, 27 participants (Avila 2024, high risk of bias); very low certainty (two levels for risk of bias and two for imprecision). The table's 11 per 1,000 and 18 per 1,000 are not the observed rates (0 of 9 and 1 of 18) and the review does not say how they were derived; the risk ratio and its interval match a 0.5 correction to each cell (editors' recalculation). Cigarettes per day among people still smoking at week 8: mean difference −1.07 (−12.72 to 10.58), 19 people with complete data.

Results › Synthesis of results › Adverse events (ONP against minimal control; ONP versus e-cigarettes; ONP versus no tobacco or nicotine product use; ONP at different doses); Summary of findings 1 and 3; Plain language summary › What did we find?

Biomarkers against minimal control (Rensch 2023, tobacco-industry funded, high risk of bias, 53 people, about one week): NNAL mean difference −265.30 ng/g creatinine (−350.64 to −179.96) from a control mean of 330; COHb −6.7% (−8.33 to −5.07) from a control mean of 11.3%; 16 further biomarkers of exposure all favoured pouches with intervals excluding no difference. Very low certainty (risk of bias, imprecision). Against a no-tobacco group (46 people) none of 18 biomarkers clearly differed. Avila 2024 (19 people) found lower exhaled carbon monoxide with pouches than continued smoking, interval including no difference.

Rensch 2023 was funded by the pouch manufacturer (a tobacco company); the other three trials by philanthropic, academic or governmental bodies. The industry trial reported no smoking outcome, no serious events, and the largest set of biomarker results; the review states that its findings were consistent with the non-industry-funded studies. The review was funded by the US National Cancer Institute and the FDA Center for Tobacco Products through CAsToR 3.0; the review says no author took part in an included trial; no author declares funding from a tobacco, pouch or e-cigarette company (some declare payments from smoking-cessation medicine makers and public bodies).
